newsitem.title: USA: US MIDWEST DIRECT HOG PRICES STEADY-OFF $1-DEALERS.
newsitem.headline: US MIDWEST DIRECT HOG PRICES STEADY-OFF $1-DEALERS.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices were steady to $1.00 per cwt lower amid light packer demand and more than adequate hog supplies, livestock dealers said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold $0.50 to $1.00 lower at $54.50 to $56.00 in the country and $56.50 to $57.00 at plants, the dealers said.
Illinois hogs sold steady to $0.50 lower at $55.00 to $56.00 in the country and $56.50 to $57.00 at plants.
Indiana hogs sold $1.00 lower at $54.50 to $55.50 in the country and $56.00 at the plants.
Ohio hogs sold steady at $54.00 to $55.00 in the country and $56.00 to $57.00 at plants, the dealers said.
"We've got a good run of hogs this morning and the packer is working hard at saving money," an Indiana hog buyer said.
Hog supplies were particularly plentiful in the western corn belt, with several packer buyers saying they were already lining up supplies for Wednesday.
Light pressure also was exerted by weak pork prices on Monday, the dealers said.
Estimated gross pork cutout values on Monday were quoted down $0.33 to $0.39 per cwt, USDA reported.
